title.title: Thomason model structures in every strict dimension
title.subtitle: Claim: strict $n$-categories, for every $n$ up to $\omega$, model all homotopy types, as categories do

plain: Can rigid algebraic gadgets, built from arrows between arrows, model every shape? Yes, in every dimension

beats.text: Do strict $n$-categories model all homotopy types, as small categories do?
Claimed for every dimension: the missing pushout condition, proved

steps: The model structure needs one thing: certain pushouts behave well
The paper proves those pushouts match pushouts of nerves
In every dimension at once, and the result is checked in Lean

voice.text: Small categories model every shape. Do strict higher categories, in any dimension, too?

Claimed: yes, for every n, up to omega.
